text: Mereological nihilism is the view that:
choices: for any objects whatsoever, there exists a further object that is their mereological sum.
composition never occurs; there are no composite objects, only mereological simples (so there is no table, only 'simples arranged tablewise').
composition occurs only when the activity of the parts constitutes a life.
an object has all of its parts essentially and so cannot survive the loss of any part.
explanation: Nihilism denies that any plurality composes a further thing, so strictly only simples exist and 'there is a table' is paraphrased as 'there are simples arranged tablewise.' Distractor 0 is its opposite (universalism) and distractor 2 is van Inwagen's restricted organicism, both of which affirm at least some composition.
